route_note: llama.cpp's own CMake build of the test-backend-ops target at the exact commits (buggy 9e0e220594, fixed 73a43d1f69), identical flags for both variants: cmake (system 3.26.5, which accepts CUDA 13.4; the cmake/4.3.4 module is unusable: libjsoncpp.so.19 missing) -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DGGML_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=89 (derived from $RW_NVCC_FLAGS; the ggml CMake turns it into --generate-code=arch=compute_89,code=[compute_89,sm_89], i.e. SASS + PTX) -DCMAKE_CUDA_FLAGS=-lineinfo -DLLAMA_BUILD_TESTS=ON -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF -DLLAMA_OPENSSL=OFF -DLLAMA_BUILD_SERVER=OFF -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DCMAKE_BUILD_RPATH='$ORIGIN', no -G (Unix Makefiles), `cmake --build --target test-backend-ops -j8` (8 min per variant). The project's Release nvcc flags are kept: -lineinfo -O3 -DNDEBUG -std=c++17 -use_fast_math -extended-lambda -compress-mode=size (fatbin sections compressed). Relocatability: ggml/llama are static libraries (BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF) so all device code is in the test-backend-ops executable; the gcc-12.4 runtime libs libstdc++.so.6, libgcc_s.so.1, libgomp.so.1 are copied next to it and found through the $ORIGIN rpath (the system libstdc++ is gcc 8 and there is no static libstdc++.a; without them the binary needs LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/ohpc/pub/compiler/gcc/12.4.0/lib64); libcudart/libcublas/libcublasLt are found through the RPATH /usr/local/cuda-13.4/targets/x86_64-linux/lib, libcuda.so.1 from the driver. Checked with env -i ldd and env -i ./test-backend-ops --help from BeeGFS. -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF builds the CPU reference backend for baseline x86-64 (no -march=native), so the binary runs on any node (it does not change the CUDA code). The source tarball is the whole tree needed by cmake (2,221 files: CMakeLists.txt cmake common ggml include licenses src tests vendor examples pocs app tools without tools/ui).
driver: test-backend-ops test -b CUDA0 -o MUL_MAT_ID -p 'type_a=q4_0,type_b=f32,n_mats=8,n_used=4,b=0,m=512,n=32,k=256' (the record's verifier-corrected quantized case; the original f16 case never reaches mm_ids_helper). It matches exactly one test case. Launches in order: mm_ids_helper<4> <<<8, 32>>> (8 experts, one warp each), quantize_mmq_q8_1, mul_mat_q<2,32,0> (mmq path).
input: random tensors generated by the test itself (init_mul_mat_id_tensors), CPU backend as reference; no files. Access estimate (ncu on the sm_75 smoke build): 1,702,409 thread-level memory instructions over the three launched kernels (all address spaces), of which mm_ids_helper<4> 1,545 (8 shared LDS + 32 shared STS warp-level instructions), quantize_mmq_q8_1 43,008, mul_mat_q 1,657,856.
